label: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics I.7, 1098a7-20: A life realizing the human good involves actual…
interpretation: The conclusion describes human good as activity of soul according to virtue, according to the best and most complete if there are several, and adds a complete life. The reading preserves activity rather than mere rational capacity and the complete-life qualification. VirtuousActivity is a parameter for the specified appropriate excellence; no ordering or independent justification of virtues is encoded. The analogy and human-function identification are not claimed to be proved.
